expect.words: West of House
You are standing in an open field west of a white house, with a boarded front door.
There is a small mailbox here.
West of House
You are standing in an open field west of a white house, with a boarded front door.
There is a small mailbox here.
Opening the small mailbox reveals a leaflet.
(Taken)
"WELCOME TO ZORK!
ZORK is a game of adventure, danger, and low cunning. In it you will explore some of the most amazing territory ever seen by mortals. No computer should be without one!"
The house is a beautiful colonial house which is painted white. It is clear that the owners must have been extremely wealthy.

The front door is solid oak and painted white, like the rest of the house, and is boarded across with planks nailed every which way, by someone in more of a hurry than a carpenter. Whatever the owners meant by it, they did not mean visitors.
The door is closed.
North of House
You are facing the north side of a white house. There is no door here, and all the windows are boarded up. To the north a narrow path winds through the trees.
Behind House
You are behind the white house. A path leads into the forest to the east. In one corner of the house there is a small window which is slightly ajar.
The window is slightly ajar, but not enough to allow entry.
With great effort, you open the window far enough to allow entry.
Kitchen

You are in the kitchen of the white house. A table seems to have been used recently for the preparation of food. A passage leads to the west and a dark staircase can be seen leading upward. A dark chimney leads down and to the east is a small window which is open.
On the table is an elongated brown sack, smelling of hot peppers.
A bottle is sitting on the table.
The glass bottle contains:
A quantity of water

The kitchen table is a sturdy, scrubbed affair of plain wood, scarred by knives and stained here and there by whatever was prepared on it recently. Someone has been eating well, and has not been tidying up.
Sitting on the kitchen table is:
A brown sack
A glass bottle
It is an elongated sack of coarse brown paper, folded over at the top and spotted with grease. It smells of hot peppers, and has clearly been somebody's lunch.
The brown sack is closed.
The chimney leads downward, and looks climbable.
Opening the brown sack reveals a lunch, and a clove of garlic.
It is a hot pepper sandwich, wrapped in waxed paper that has long since given up trying to contain it. It smells of hot peppers from across the room, and of more hot peppers from closer to.
It is a single clove of garlic, plump and papery and very much itself. It is the sort of thing that keeps certain company at a distance, and most other company too.
Taken.
Taken.
Living Room

You are in the living room. There is a doorway to the east, a wooden door with strange gothic lettering to the west, which appears to be nailed shut, a trophy case, and a large oriental rug in the center of the room.
A battery-powered brass lantern is on the trophy case.
Above the trophy case hangs an elvish sword of great antiquity.
The engravings translate to "This space intentionally left blank."
It is a large oriental rug, very fine and very heavy, laid squarely in the center of the room. It lies a little unevenly, as if something beneath it were not quite flat.
The trophy case is a handsome thing of polished wood and glass, fastened securely to the wall and plainly built to hold treasures. It has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.
The trophy case is empty.
The blade is long, keen and elvish, its hilt worked with vines and runes. It is very old, and has plainly been in worse places than a living room.
It is a battery-powered brass lantern, dented here and there but sound, with a stout handle and a glass that someone has kept clean.
The lamp is turned off.
Taken.
Taken.
With a great effort, the rug is moved to one side of the room, revealing the dusty cover of a closed trap door.
The brass lantern is now on.

It is a square trap door of heavy planks, set flush into the floor where the rug used to hide it, with an iron ring to lift it by. A good deal of dust has settled on it, and nobody has disturbed it lately.
The trap door is closed.
The door reluctantly opens to reveal a rickety staircase descending into darkness.
The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
Cellar
You are in a dark and damp cellar with a narrow passageway leading north, and a crawlway to the south. On the west is the bottom of a steep metal ramp which is unclimbable.
Your sword is glowing with a faint blue glow.
The bottom of a steep metal ramp comes down out of the dark on the west side of the cellar. It is polished smooth by everything that has ever slid down it, and it is unclimbable.
The Troll Room
This is a small room with passages to the east and south and a forbidding hole leading west. Bloodstains and deep scratches (perhaps made by an axe) mar the walls.
A nasty-looking troll, brandishing a bloody axe, blocks all passages out of the room.
Your sword has begun to glow very brightly.

The troll is squat, greenish and nearly as wide as he is tall, with small red eyes and a great many teeth, not all of them his own. The bloody axe is clenched in his fist, and he swings it idly back and forth, the way other people tap a foot. He is watching you the way a cook watches a chicken.

expect.text: troll_room.troll woke, 60 seconds after it asked

expect.words: The axe sweeps past as you jump aside.
You charge, but the troll jumps nimbly aside.
The troll swings his axe, and it nicks your arm as you dodge.
Your sword misses the troll by an inch.
The flat of the troll's axe hits you delicately on the head, knocking you out.
Conquering his fears, the troll puts you to death.
It appears that that last blow was too much for you. I'm afraid you are dead.
**** You have died ****
Now, let's take a look here... Well, you probably deserve another chance. I can't quite fix you up completely, but you can't have everything.
Your belongings, such as they were, have not come with you. They are scattered about the Empire, though somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.
Forest
This is a forest, with trees in all directions. To the east, there appears to be sunlight.
Forest Path
This is a path winding through a dimly lit forest. The path heads north-south here. One particularly large tree with some low branches stands at the edge of the path.

expect.text: troll_room.troll woke, 60 seconds after it asked

expect.words: It is a particularly large tree, older than the house and in no hurry, with some low branches that all but invite climbing.
Up a Tree
You are about 10 feet above the ground nestled among some large branches. The nearest branch above you is above your reach.
Beside you on the branch is a small bird's nest.

In the bird's nest is a large egg encrusted with precious jewels, apparently scavenged by a childless songbird. The egg is covered with fine gold inlay, and ornamented in lapis lazuli and mother-of-pearl. Unlike most eggs, this one is hinged and closed with a delicate looking clasp. The egg appears extremely fragile.
The nest is a neat cup of twigs, grass and down, wedged into the fork of a branch by a songbird with better taste in treasure than in architecture.
The bird's nest contains:
A jewel-encrusted egg

The egg is covered with fine gold inlay and ornamented in lapis lazuli and mother-of-pearl. Unlike most eggs, it is hinged, and closed with a delicate looking clasp. It looks extremely fragile, and extremely valuable, in that order.
The jewel-encrusted egg is closed.
Taken.
Forest Path
North of House
There is a sword here.
Behind House
A small leaflet is on the ground.
Kitchen
Living Room
There is a brass lantern (battery-powered) here.
Taken.
The trophy case isn't open.

Behind House
A small leaflet is on the ground.

There is a sword here.

expect.words: Kitchen
Living Room
Opened.
It is already on.
Done.
The door reluctantly opens to reveal a rickety staircase descending into darkness.
The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
Cellar
Your sword is glowing with a faint blue glow.
The Troll Room
A nasty-looking troll, brandishing a bloody axe, blocks all passages out of the room.
Your sword has begun to glow very brightly.
Clang! Crash! The troll parries.
The troll hits you with a glancing blow, and you are momentarily stunned.
You are still recovering from that last blow, so your attack is ineffective.
The axe sweeps past as you jump aside.
The troll takes a fatal blow and slumps to the floor dead.
Almost as soon as the troll breathes his last breath, a cloud of sinister black fog envelops him, and when the fog lifts, the carcass has disappeared.
Your sword is no longer glowing.
The Troll Room
This is a small room with passages to the east and south and a forbidding hole leading west. Bloodstains and deep scratches (perhaps made by an axe) mar the walls.
There is a bloody axe here.
The bloodstains are old and brown and spattered high up the walls. Whoever they belonged to has no further use for them.
Deep scratches score the rock, the kind made by something heavy swung hard and often. An axe would do it. Someone has evidently been practicing.

The hole in the west wall is ragged and dark, dark even by the standards of this place. Beyond it the rock is cut into narrow passages that twist away out of sight almost at once. It is not so much an exit as a suggestion, and not a friendly one.
The axe is a heavy, ugly, single-bitted thing, its haft wrapped in greasy leather and its edge notched from use. The blood on the blade is not all old.
Taken.
East-West Passage
This is a narrow east-west passageway. There is a narrow stairway leading down at the north end of the room.
A narrow stairway goes down at the north end of the passage, cut into the rock in steps worn hollow in the middle by a great many feet, none of them recent.
Round Room
This is a circular stone room with passages in all directions. Several of them have unfortunately been blocked by cave-ins.

Fallen rock fills most of the passages out of the room, ceiling and all. In the passage to the south somebody has started clearing it: the rubble is sorted into neat heaps, smallest nearest, as though its sorter had stepped out for a moment, some time ago.

Passages leave the room in every direction, like spokes from a hub. Most of them do not get far. The ones that do go east, west, north and southeast; the one to the south looks as though it means to, and is being helped.

Fallen rock fills most of the passages out of the room, ceiling and all. In the passage to the south somebody has started clearing it: the rubble is sorted into neat heaps, smallest nearest, as though its sorter had stepped out for a moment, some time ago.

The passage south narrows almost at once and then stops, choked by one of the cave-ins. Somebody has made a start on clearing it: the rubble is sorted into neat heaps by size, smallest nearest. Whoever it was has not finished, and you decide not to be the one who does.
You can't move the cave-ins.
Loud Room

This is a large room with a ceiling which cannot be detected from the ground. There is a narrow passage from east to west and a stone stairway leading upward. The room is deafeningly loud with an undetermined rushing sound. The sound seems to reverberate from all of the walls, making it difficult even to think.
On the ground is a large platinum bar.
Bar bar ...
Bar bar ...
Listen listen ...
Stairs stairs ...
The acoustics of the room change subtly.
Taken.

It is a bar of platinum the size of a house brick and very nearly the weight of one, cast plain and stamped with nothing at all, as though whoever made it felt the metal said enough. It is cold to the touch, and quite silent, which in this room is a distinction.
Loud Room
This is a large room with a ceiling which cannot be detected from the ground. There is a narrow passage from east to west and a stone stairway leading upward. The room is eerie in its quietness.
A stone stairway climbs out of the room, steep and uneven, toward somewhere with less noise in it.
You hear nothing out of the ordinary.
Damp Cave
This cave has exits to the west and east, and narrows to a crack toward the south. The earth is particularly damp here.
The crack is a dark slit in the rock a few inches wide, narrowing as it goes. A draught comes out of it, and so, now and then, does an ant.

The earth underfoot is particularly damp, as the room promised, and gives a little under your weight. Something has dripped here for a very long time without ever quite getting around to being a puddle.

The passage east comes out on a ledge high above a broad, cold river that is going somewhere in a hurry. There is no way down that does not involve the river at the bottom of it, and without a boat that is as far as this way goes.
Damp Cave
This cave has exits to the west and east, and narrows to a crack toward the south. The earth is particularly damp here.
Loud Room
Deep Canyon
You are on the south edge of a deep canyon. Passages lead off to the east, northwest and southwest. A stairway leads down. You can hear the sound of flowing water from below.
The canyon falls away to the north, sheer and black, too deep for your light to find the bottom. From somewhere far below comes the sound of water, going about its business.
You hear nothing out of the ordinary.

The passage east climbs toward a deep, steady hum, the sound of a great deal of water being held back by something that would rather not be disturbed. A board is nailed across it: "FLOOD CONTROL DAM #3. CLOSED FOR INSPECTION. -- The Management." You leave the dam to its inspection.

The passage northwest grows wet underfoot, and then wetter, and then you can hear a great deal of water lying very still somewhere ahead. A board is nailed across the passage at shin height: "RESERVOIR CLOSED. -- Flood Control Dam #3, by order of the Management." You step back over the puddle you were standing in.
North-South Passage
This is a high north-south passage, which forks to the northeast.
The passage is high and narrow, a slot in the rock that runs north and south, with a fork going off to the northeast as if it had had second thoughts. The ceiling is lost in the dark overhead.
Round Room
Engravings Cave
You have entered a low cave with passages leading northwest and east.
There are old engravings on the walls here.

The engravings were incised in the living rock of the cave wall by an unknown hand. They depict, in symbolic form, the beliefs of the ancient Zorkers. Skillfully interwoven with the bas reliefs are excerpts illustrating the major religious tenets of that time. Unfortunately, a later age seems to have considered them blasphemous and just as skillfully excised them.
The walls of the cave are cut all over with old engravings, in a style that took its time and expected to be looked at.
Dome Room
You are at the periphery of a large dome, which forms the ceiling of another room below. Protecting you from a precipitous drop is a wooden railing which circles the dome.

The railing is of dark, polished wood, waist-high, running all the way round the edge of the dome. Beyond it is a precipitous drop to the floor of a room below, a good twenty feet down. The railing is very solid. It is the most reassuring thing you have seen in some time.
The dome curves away beneath you, a great bowl of smooth stone with the railing round its rim. It is the ceiling of a room below, seen, unusually, from above.
That sentence isn't one I recognize.
You cannot go down without fracturing many bones.
You are carrying:
A brass lantern (providing light)
A sword
A bloody axe
A platinum bar
Engravings Cave
There are old engravings on the walls here.
Round Room
East-West Passage
Chasm
A chasm runs southwest to northeast and the path follows it. You are on the south side of the chasm, where a crack opens into a passage.
The chasm runs southwest to northeast, a black slot in the floor of the world, too deep for any light to find the bottom. A cold air comes up out of it, smelling of nothing at all.
The crack in the south side of the chasm is wide enough for a person, just, and opens into a passage that leads away south.

The path follows the chasm northeast toward a smell of standing water, and stops at a cord strung across it between two spikes. From the cord hangs a card: "RESERVOIR SOUTH. CLOSED. -- The Management." You go back the way you came.
East-West Passage
Chasm
North-South Passage
Deep Canyon
North-South Passage
Round Room
East-West Passage
The Troll Room
Cellar

The crawlway to the south is low and mean, the kind of tunnel that is wider at the mouth than it ever is again. Someone has cleared it lately: the fallen rock is stacked neatly along one side, and there are fresh pick marks in the roof.
East of Chasm
You are on the east edge of a chasm, the bottom of which cannot be seen. A narrow passage goes north, and the path you are on continues to the east.

The chasm drops away from your feet into a dark that your lamp does not so much light as annoy. A pebble kicked over the edge is never heard from again. Neither, by the look of it, was whoever kicked the last one.
Gallery
This is an art gallery. Most of the paintings have been stolen by vandals with exceptional taste. The vandals left through either the north or west exits.
Fortunately, there is still one chance for you to be a vandal, for on the far wall is a painting of unparalleled beauty.

It is a painting of a sunlit valley, done with such tenderness that it is hard to look at it for long, and harder to look away. The signature in the corner is too modest to read. The artist was a neglected genius, and it shows.
Your load is too heavy.
The surrounding wall is solid, plain and entirely uninterested in you.
Studio

This appears to have been an artist's studio. The walls and floors are splattered with paints of 69 different colors. Strangely enough, nothing of value is hanging here. At the south end of the room is an open door (also covered with paint). A dark and narrow chimney leads up from a fireplace; although you might be able to get up it, it seems unlikely you could get back down.
Loosely attached to a wall is a small piece of paper.
(Taken)
Congratulations!

You are the privileged owner of ZORK I: The Great Underground Empire, a self-contained and self-maintaining universe. If used and maintained in accordance with normal operating practices for small universes, ZORK will provide many months of trouble-free operation.
The chimney is dark and narrow and leads up out of the fireplace. You might just get up it, if you travelled light and had a light to travel by. Getting back down it is another matter.
Dropped.
Gallery
Fortunately, there is still one chance for you to be a vandal, for on the far wall is a painting of unparalleled beauty.
Taken.
East of Chasm
Cellar
The door is locked from above.
East of Chasm
Gallery
Studio
There is a bloody axe here.
You can't get up there with what you're carrying. The chimney has room for you, a light to climb by and one thing more, and not an inch besides.
Dropped.
You leave, and take what you carry with you.
